title: Phone messages and calls
summary: phone.text shows a message toast from a contact; phone.call places a real incoming call from an active journal contact with timed subtitle lines, a ring time and optional auto-answer; phone.end and phone.state end and read it.

demand.note: Messages and calls from contacts, including new XF contacts; script can't create journal entries.

rows.note: An unknown contact refused, nothing rang.
Answered with T; ring_s was ignored then (fixed in 0.8.18).
The speaker is the contact's name, not its id.

limits: Only an active journal contact can call; an unknown caller is refused. A journal-free caller card is left out (RB-224).
quirks: Contact names in phone.state were unresolved LocKeys in Borg 1.

known_issues.summary: The call route (questTriggerCallRequest with its state polled from a fact) and the journal-free message toast are source and offline only beyond Borg 1 and 3's rows.

title: An XF quest in the tracker
summary: quest.set, quest.objective and quest.clear put an XF quest with objectives in the game's own tracker, never the journal, with areas that complete an objective; quest.state reads it.

demand.note: Objectives in the journal or an XF tracker (a journal-free tracker).

rows.note: The objectives showed in reverse order; fixed in 0.8.14.
Two objectives in order, and the order held after one was done.

title: XF map pins
summary: world.pin places an XF map pin (world map, minimap and in the world) at a point, above a showroom head or above V, with an ink-drawn XF mark that stays at the screen's edge when the pin is off screen; world.pin.clear removes them.

demand.note: Map pins and areas: a test pin today.

rows.note: No XF mark in the world; fixed in 0.8.3.
The mark at the side edges, by the coordinator's captures.

limits: At most 8 pins; a temporary test feature.

known_issues.summary: Pin entries' mark fields are written from the UI's worker threads while the game thread may change the registry.
The HUD blocks the mark avoids are a measured template, not the live HUD.

title: Notifications
summary: notify.show and notify.hide put up the game's warning banner, the centred message, the quest toasts and a subtitle line, removable by the bridge.

demand.note: Messages to the player (notifications in the DM toolkit).

rows.note: All four shown; onscreen drew at the left edge, moved to the cinematic message position in 0.8.14.

limits: The shard popup and the experience toast are left out (RB-224).

title: In-game watchers
summary: watch.arm arms watchers polled in the game (enter, leave, gaze, weapon, combat, vehicle, interact, choice, timer, clock), each firing up to eight micro-actions through the dispatcher's own gates, without the agent.

demand.note: DM watchers for V's own state are part of the event feed.

rows.note: A weapon watcher fired on weapon.draw and ran both micro-actions.

title: The game digest
summary: game.digest reads V, the world, what the bridge placed and changed, watchers, quests, the phone and recent events in one call.
notes: Borg 1 used it throughout in place of DK1 to DK3, and a 2 s digest poller was the first watcher before the recorder.

title: The DM toolkit's release
summary: Everything the live-direction toolkit brings in or changes is put back by the kill switch, the pause, a handover or loading a save; a door or vehicle changed and changed back by hand holds nothing.

rows.note: After a load with a crate, tracker and a ringing call, everything released.

known_issues.summary: Vehicle lock changes keep ownership and the save hold until a save loads, since the lock baseline can't be read back.

title: Setting quest facts
summary: Set quest facts, and keep XF's own facts in a namespace the game won't confuse with its own.

demand.note: Read and set quest facts; keep XF's own (read only today).

unknowns.question: May the bridge write vanilla state at all in release builds?
unknowns.settle_by: The maintainer's decision O5 (XF Core owned scope)

title: Scanner text
summary: Our own scanner entries for people and props, so V's scan of a staged person or object reads a line the director wrote.

demand.note: Three routes known offline (TweakXL records with a scanning component, run-time events, rewriting chunks), none seen in game.

title: Rewards and costs
summary: Give or take money, items, street cred and fixer standing as a story's outcome.

demand.note: Money, items, street cred and fixer standing.
